proposals.evidence: Andersen's aham line says 'see hakam'; the hakam pronoun paradigm labels the Gujarra aham as nominative singular 'I' and compares RV/Pali ahaṁ. Turner 992 ahám 'I' explicitly lists Ashokan shah./gir. ahaṁ beside hakaṁ.

proposals.evidence: Andersen's separately bounded yā- verb means 'to go, to go on' and compares RV yāti and Pali yāti, with an inscriptional participial form. Turner 10452 yā́ti 'goes, approaches, comes to' explicitly lists Pali yāti and Ashokan yāti/yaṁti.

proposals.evidence: Andersen's hu- verb means 'to be, become', compares RV bhavati and Pali hoti, and lists inscriptional hoti/hota/hotu. Turner 9416 bhávati 'becomes, is' explicitly lists Pali hōti and Ashokan shah./man./kāl. hoti.
